title: Forged committer dates can make history-based --at count early
description: Review of faq3.12 (2026-10-23): query --at (tiers since faq3.11, endorsements since faq3.12) uses the first-parent committer date to decide what was in effect at TIME. A fast-forwarded contributor commit with a forged GIT_COMMITTER_DATE can make a tier or endorsement count earlier than it was merged. Cheapest fix: clamp each first-parent commit's effective date to at least its first-parent ancestor's (monotonic), so a backdated commit cannot precede what came before it; alternatively require --no-ff merges into the registry (process, not code). Decide and record in DESIGN TRQP bridge Time.
acceptance_criteria: Test: a commit with a committer date earlier than its parent's does not make its records count before the parent's date; DESIGN states the rule.
